claims.text: Single-phase ZrB2 typically requires processing above 2300 °C to achieve full density.
Adding SiC to ZrB2 before sintering can enable manufacture below 1700 °C.
SiC addition improves densification of ZrB2 at lower sintering temperatures.
SiC addition improves grain-boundary bonding in ZrB2.
SiC lowers the activation energy for densification through transient liquid-phase formation.
SiC assists densification by scavenging interfacial oxides.
Oxidation of SiC during high-temperature service forms a protective silica-based surface layer.
The silica-based surface layer restricts oxygen ingress into the composite.
The silica-based surface layer retards attack by liquid plating metal.
ZrB2-SiC processed below 1700 °C will attain full density.
The resulting ZrB2-SiC composite will have mechanical strength comparable to or greater than conventional high-temperature, single-phase ZrB2.
The resulting ZrB2-SiC composite will exhibit significantly better oxidation resistance than conventional high-temperature, single-phase ZrB2 and prior lower-temperature specimens.
The resulting ZrB2-SiC composite will suffer less liquid plating-metal corrosion than conventional high-temperature, single-phase ZrB2 and prior lower-temperature specimens.
SiC addition will improve mechanical-integrity retention during oxidation and liquid-metal exposure.
The predicted oxidation benefit applies at service temperatures up to approximately 1500 °C.
The predicted corrosion benefit applies during continuous or prolonged contact with molten plating metal.
Previously reported lower-temperature ZrB2 specimens are deficient in densification, oxidation durability, and corrosion resistance.
